title: Biochemistry I: Proteins, Enzymes & Metabolism
description: A mechanistic and quantitative introduction to protein structure, enzyme kinetics, thermodynamics, central metabolism, and pathway regulation.

prerequisites.statement: General Chemistry II; Organic Chemistry I recommended

outcomes.description: Interpret protein sequence, structure, and binding models.
Track carbon, electrons, and energy through central metabolism.
Explain pathway control through multiple regulatory layers.

lesson_objectives.description: Distinguish binding affinity, specificity, and cooperativity.
Distinguish competitive and noncompetitive model signatures.
Use catalytic efficiency and model assumptions carefully.
Track oxidation state and carbon fate through glycolysis and respiration.
Relate redox carriers and proton motive force to ATP synthesis.
Identify control at substrate supply, allostery, covalent modification, and expression.
Predict how perturbing one pathway affects connected fluxes.

workload.basis: Not measured. Legacy nominal credit and display-time labels are not retained as workload estimates.

lessons.title: Protein structure and molecular recognition
lessons.worked_example: For a 1:1 interaction at free ligand concentration [L] = Kd, fractional occupancy θ = [L]/(Kd + [L]) = 0.5.

lessons.title: Enzyme mechanisms and inhibition
lessons.worked_example: If competitive inhibitor raises apparent Km from 2 to 8 mM while Vmax remains 100 μmol/min, sufficiently high substrate can still approach the same Vmax.

lessons.title: Bioenergetics and central carbon metabolism
lessons.worked_example: Net glycolysis produces 2 ATP and 2 NADH per glucose. If a preparation yields 3 ATP per cytosolic NADH via its chosen shuttle, glycolytic reducing equivalents contribute 6 ATP equivalents in that accounting scheme.

lessons.title: Pathway regulation and metabolic integration
lessons.worked_example: If a labeled-carbon pool stays constant while labeled product appearance slows, both production and consumption may have changed; isotope time courses help separate those rates.
